programs.title: Applied Artificial Intelligence
programs.award: Certificate of Achievement requiring 8S/12Q to fewer than 16S/24Q units
outcomes: Discuss artificial intelligence (AI) core concepts and explain the fundamentals of AI applications
Design and utilize effective prompts for Large Language Models, which includes understanding and usage of major prompt patterns, Retrieval Augmented Generation, AI agent and customized GPT
Evaluate, design and implement responsible and ethical AI solutions with transparency and accountability

programs.title: Applied Mathematics
programs.award: Certificate of Achievement requiring 8S/12Q to fewer than 16S/24Q units
outcomes: Apply statistical and probabilistic methods to model and analyze real-world phenomena in science, engineering and technology
Solve first- and higher-order differential equations using analytical, numerical and qualitative techniques relevant to modeling dynamic systems
Analyze complex data sets using techniques from engineering statistics, including control charts, design of experiments and quality improvement tools
Integrate concepts from statistics and differential equations to formulate mathematical models and interpret their solutions in applied contexts
Design and complete a special project in applied mathematics that involves mathematical modeling, computational tools and critical evaluation of results
Communicate applied mathematical reasoning, findings and modeling outcomes

programs.title: Business Administration 2.0

programs.title: Community Impact
programs.award: Certificate of Achievement requiring 8S/12Q to fewer than 16S/24Q units
outcomes: Analyze the impediments to community strength

programs.title: Elementary Mathematics Education
programs.award: Certificate of Achievement requiring 8S/12Q to fewer than 16S/24Q units
outcomes: Display increasing confidence in their ability to use a range of speaking, listening and collaboration skills
Explain fundamental mathematical concepts—including number systems, operations, algebra, geometry and probability—in a way that supports conceptual understanding for elementary learners
Design and relate messages clearly for effective and appropriate oral communication
Apply problem-solving strategies and mathematical reasoning to real-world scenarios relevant to elementary education and everyday decision-making

Analyze, evaluate and respond competently to discourse by weighing research, examining evidence and using critical reasoning; use visual models, manipulatives and representations to support mathematical thinking and communication, particularly in the context of elementary math instruction
Demonstrate fluency with key topics from finite mathematics and liberal arts math, including logic, set theory, combinatorics and basic financial mathematics
Interpret and analyze data using basic statistical techniques relevant to classroom assessment and educational research
Communicate mathematical ideas clearly and accurately using appropriate language, notation and pedagogical techniques for diverse learners

programs.title: Journalism
outcomes: Demonstrate competency in the basics of journalistic writing, including grammar, punctuation, story structure and journalistic styles
Demonstrate competency in research, information gathering and critical analysis of information using techniques such as observation, researching sources and interviewing
Compile a portfolio of print, electronic and/or multimedia projects that tell journalistic stories
Apply media literacy skills to explain the communication process and detect media bias

programs.title: Law, Public Policy, and Society
outcomes: Define and analyze the discipline of philosophy with a sustained focus on the ethics branch of philosophy

programs.title: Mathematics for Business and Social Sciences
programs.award: Certificate of Achievement requiring 8S/12Q to fewer than 16S/24Q units
outcomes: Apply statistical techniques to analyze data and make informed decisions in business and social science contexts
Solve problems involving systems of equations, linear programming, matrices and logic as they relate to business and social sciences
Use concepts from business calculus—including marginal analysis, optimization and exponential growth/decay—to model and interpret real-world scenarios
Integrate quantitative methods from multiple disciplines to develop and interpret models relevant to finance, economics, management or social policy
Complete a capstone project involving a real-world application of mathematical tools to a business or social science problem, including data analysis and modeling

programs.title: Statistics
programs.award: Certificate of Achievement requiring 8S/12Q to fewer than 16S/24Q units
outcomes: Interpret and summarize univariate and multivariate data using appropriate descriptive statistics and graphical displays
Apply statistical methods such as hypothesis testing, confidence intervals, regression and ANOVA to analyze data in scientific, social and engineering contexts
Use computational tools and statistical software to perform data analysis and simulation, emphasizing reproducibility and accuracy
Design and execute a statistical investigation, including data collection, cleaning, modeling and interpretation, demonstrating awareness of ethical considerations
Evaluate critically the statistical arguments presented in academic studies, media or professional reports by identifying assumptions, limitations and potential sources of bias
